items.text: voľný čas = free time
items.picture: A sunny Saturday afternoon on the grass by the Danube: Emma lies on her front reading a book with her shoes off, Lucia dozes in the sun beside her, and Tomáš throws a frisbee to Marek.

items.text: Čo rada robíš vo voľnom čase? = What do you like doing in your free time? (to a woman)
koníček = hobby
kresliť a fotografovať = to draw and to take photos
items.picture: Two halves on the square in the Old Town, by the fountain. Left: Emma sits on the fountain's edge, drawing the pastel houses in a sketchbook. Right: Lucia crouches to take a photo of the same houses with a camera.

items.text: oddychovať a pozerať televíziu = to relax and to watch TV
items.picture: Evening at home: Tomáš lies stretched out on a sofa in his socks, a cushion behind his head and a bowl of crisps on his chest, watching TV.

items.text: hrať na gitare = to play the guitar
nákupné centrum = shopping centre
items.picture: Inside a big, bright shopping centre with shops on two floors, escalators and a glass roof: Emma and Lucia sit at a small café table on the upper floor, shopping bags at their feet.

items.text: stretávať sa s priateľmi = to meet up with friends
items.picture: Saturday afternoon at the fountain on the square in the Old Town: Lucia, Tomáš and Marek are already waiting; Emma arrives and waves, and Lucia goes to hug her.

items.text: How do you say “At the weekend I meet up with friends”?
Rád ťa počujem. = Good to hear from you. (a man speaking)
items.picture: Split picture of a phone call. Left: Tomáš walks along the Danube embankment with his phone to his ear, beaming. Right: Lucia, at her desk in the dorm room, answers, delighted to hear from him.

items.text: Tomáš calls Lucia. How does she greet him?
Máš chuť ísť do kina? = Do you fancy going to the cinema?
plaváreň a sauna = swimming pool and sauna
items.picture: An indoor swimming pool with lanes under a high glass wall. Emma swims front crawl fast down one lane, with Tomáš far behind her in the next, impressed. Through a glass door at the side, Lucia sits in a wooden sauna, wrapped in a towel and red-cheeked.

items.text: plavky = swimsuit, swimming trunks
items.picture: In the dorm room, Emma packs her sports bag for the pool: she holds up her swimsuit, with a rolled towel and goggles beside the bag on her bed.

items.text: To znie dobre! = That sounds good!
Platí! = Deal!
items.picture: In the café near the university, Tomáš holds out his hand across the table and Emma shakes it with a grin, while Lucia, beside her, gives a thumbs up: the plan is agreed.

items.text: Tomáš asks: “Ideš v sobotu s nami na plaváreň?” Which answer means yes?
Môžeš s nami počítať. = You can count on us.
Emma thanks Tomáš for the invitation. What does she say?
Máš v piatok čas? = Are you free on Friday?
Bohužiaľ nemôžem. = Unfortunately I can't.
items.picture: Split picture of a phone call. Left: Lucia, at her desk in the dorm room, phone to her ear, asks hopefully. Right: Marek, in his white chef's jacket in the busy kitchen of his restaurant, holds the phone between ear and shoulder while stirring a big pot, and pulls an apologetic face.

items.text: Lucia invites Marek to a games evening on Friday, but he has to work. What does he say?
To je škoda. = That's a pity.
items.picture: In the dorm room, Lucia holds up a board game she has ready for Friday and sighs with disappointment, as Emma, pulling on her coat, shakes her head apologetically.

items.text: Emma can't come on Friday. What does Lucia say to that?
upiecť tortu = to bake a cake
items.picture: In the narrow kitchen of his flat, Marek, in his red flannel shirt and an apron, flour on his hands, lifts a round cake out of the oven and smiles at the smell.

items.text: Ja to nemusím. = It's not my thing.
items.picture: In Marek's living room, Tomáš and Marek leap up from the sofa, cheering at a football match on the TV, while Lucia, curled up at the end of the sofa with a book, rolls her eyes.

items.text: Futbal? Ja to nemusím. What does Lucia mean?
Mám alergiu na mačky. = I'm allergic to cats.
items.picture: In the hallway of a friend's flat, a fluffy grey cat rubs against Lucia's legs and she sneezes hard into a tissue, her eyes red and watery, while Emma scoops the cat away.

items.text: You can't come to Lucia's games evening. What do you say to her?
Lucia doesn't like football. Which sentence says so?
športovať = to do sport
bicyklovať sa = to cycle
hrať volejbal = to play volleyball
items.picture: On a sand volleyball court by the Danube, Tomáš leaps at the net to smash the ball, Marek beside him; on the other side, Emma and Lucia dive for it.

items.text: plavec, plavkyňa = swimmer (a man, a woman)
Emma swims really well. What does Tomáš tell her?
čerstvý vzduch = fresh air
cvičiť jogu = to do yoga
items.picture: In the dorm room, on mats between the beds, Lucia holds a calm yoga pose, balancing on one leg, while Emma tries to copy her and wobbles.

items.text: lyžovať sa = to ski
items.picture: On a sunny, snowy slope in the mountains, Tomáš skis down with ease, spraying snow; further up the slope, Emma stands on skis for the first time, arms out, wobbling.

items.text: Emma has never learned to ski. How does she say “I can't ski”?
korčuľovať sa = to skate
zimný štadión = ice rink
items.picture: The ice rink: a big indoor hall with a curved roof, white ice inside low boards and rows of seats around it. Skaters circle the ice; Lucia skates backwards, holding both of Emma's hands as Emma takes her first wobbly glides. By the boards, a counter hires out skates.

items.text: spadnúť = to fall (down)
items.picture: On the ice rink, Emma's legs fly out from under her and she lands on the ice with a thump; Lucia skates up to her, trying not to laugh.

items.text: modrina = bruise
items.picture: Back in the dorm room, Emma sits on her bed and rolls up her jeans to show Lucia a big blue-purple bruise on her knee; Lucia winces.

items.text: Som úplne hotová. = I'm completely worn out. (a woman speaking)
Som úplne hotová. What does Emma mean?
výlet = trip, outing
items.picture: A day trip: Emma, Lucia, Tomáš and Marek, with backpacks, walk a path over a wooded hilltop, a castle ruin on the next hill ahead; Emma, in front, spreads her arms and breathes in the fresh air.

items.text: plagát = poster
items.picture: Emma and Lucia stop at a noticeboard at the university to look at a big colourful poster with a picture of a gorilla on it; smaller posters around it show a concert and a painting. The posters have pictures only, no writing.

items.text: zoo = zoo
items.picture: Bratislava's zoo on a wooded hillside: Emma and Lucia stand among visitors at the big glass wall of the gorilla enclosure, where a big gorilla sits looking back at them; in the next enclosure monkeys swing on ropes, and a giraffe peers over the trees beyond.

items.text: Zoo: otvorené denne od 9:00 do 17:00 When can you visit?
zviera = animal
Gorily a opice sú v zoo veľká atrakcia. What does this mean?
výstava = exhibition
Študenti majú zľavu. What does the poster say?
zbierať = to collect
items.picture: In the porter's lodge, pán Kováč proudly opens a thick album full of rows of colourful postage stamps for Emma; more albums are stacked high on the shelf behind him, and Emma stares, amazed.

items.text: poštová známka = postage stamp
Pán Kováč zbiera známky už štyridsať rokov. What does this mean?
To je neuveriteľné! = That's unbelievable!
Mr Kováč has five thousand stamps. What does Emma say?
šach a karty = chess and cards
items.picture: Lucia's games evening in the dorm kitchen: at one end of the table, Tomáš plays chess with Emma, frowning in concentration; at the other end, Lucia deals out cards.

items.text: spoločenská hra = board game
items.picture: Later at the games evening in the dorm kitchen, Emma, Lucia and Tomáš sit round a board game with a big board, lots of little pieces and cards; Tomáš frowns over a long rule booklet while Emma scratches her head.

items.text: zložitý = complicated
nechať = to leave (something somewhere)
items.picture: Friday afternoon at the porter's lodge, the big clock on the wall at five: Marek, in his white chef's jacket under an open coat, sets a cake box down on the ledge of the lodge window and hurries off to work, waving; pán Kováč nods to him.

items.text: Mimochodom, kde je torta? What is Lucia asking?
prázdna krabica = an empty box
items.picture: In the porter's lodge, the big clock on the wall at seven: pán Kováč, back at his desk, lifts the lid of the cake box and stares into it. It is empty but for a few crumbs.

items.text: zmiznúť = to disappear
svedok = witness
items.picture: In the dormitory corridor, pán Kováč, playing detective with a magnifying glass and a notebook, questions Emma; she points down the corridor, remembering what she saw.

items.text: Pán Kováč hľadá zlodeja. What does this mean?
hnedý = brown
items.picture: Friday evening in the dormitory corridor: Emma, her skates over her shoulder, glimpses Filip hurrying round a corner, a young man with long straight brown hair falling over his face.

items.text: brada = beard; chin
items.picture: Tomáš stands at a bathroom mirror and proudly trims his neat short black beard with small scissors.

items.text: Filip, a new student on the second floor, is tichý a hanblivý. What is he like?
items.picture: In the dorm kitchen, Lucia chats away cheerfully to Filip, the new student; Filip looks at his feet, his hair over his face and his hands in his hoodie pocket, and says nothing.

items.text: pes = dog
items.picture: In Filip's dorm room, Filip's dog sits in a basket beside the bed, wagging its tail, a food bowl next to it; Filip kneels to stroke it.

items.text: chovať psa = to keep a dog
Prepáčte, pán Kováč! Môj pes zjedol tortu. Filip says this. Who ate the cake?
items.picture: At the porter's lodge, Filip, red-faced, holds up his dog, its nose white with cream, and apologises to pán Kováč, who stands with his arms folded and a stern frown.

items.text: Si nahnevaný? = Are you angry? (to a man)
Filip hardly says a word. Which word describes him?
